newsitem.title: Australia: TIMELINES - Today in History - Nov 7.
newsitem.headline: TIMELINES - Today in History - Nov 7.

text.p: ** BIRTHDAYS **

Polish-born physicist MARIE CURIE was born in 1867. With her husband PIERRE CURIE, she discovered radium and they had a standard unit of radium measurement named after them (the curie). Years after her husband's death MARIE received the Nobel Prize in 1911.
Australia's first woman lawyer FLOS GREIG was born in 1880. She was responsible for the Victorian Parliament passing the "FLOS GREIG Enabling Bill", which allowed women to practice law.
American screenwriter HERMAN J. MANKIEWICZ, who collaborated with ORSON WELLS on the screenplay for the Oscar-winning "Citizen KANE", was born in 1897.
South African anti-apartheid and civil rights campaigner HELEN SUZMAN was born in 1917.
American evangelist BILLY GRAHAM was born in 1918. He pioneered television evangelism and preached to million during worldwide crusades. His first crusade was Youth for Christ in 1949.

Australian operatic soprano DAME JOAN SUTHERLAND was born in 1926. She went to England in 1951 and made her debut the next year in "The Magic Flute". After achieving worldwide acclaim she retired from the stage in 1990. She usually performed under the baton of her husband, conductor RICHARD BONYNGE.

British singer, guitarist and songwriter SHARLEEN SPITERI was born in 1967. She was a member of 'Texas' who released their first record in 1987. They came to prominence as U2s support group. The first hit was "Don't Go" in 1988.
** EVENTS **
1659 : The Franco-Spanish war ended.
American singer with 'PETER, PAUL & MARY', MARY TRAVERS was born in 1937. In the 1970s she released three solo albums.

Canadian singer, guitarist and songwriter JONI MITCHELL (ROBERTA JOAN ANDERSON). Her hits include "Big Yellow Taxi" (1970) and "Help Me" (1974). She collaborated with JAME TAYLOR on "You've Got A Friend". In 1988 she released one of her best albums with "Chalk Mark In A Rain Storm".
1865 : The first pocket lighter was manufactured by the
Repeating Light Company of Springfield, Massachusetts.
1872 : The U.S. cargo ship Mary Celeste set sail from
New York on a journey which ended when it was found mysteriously abandoned the following month.
1885 : The coast-to-coast Canadian Pacific railway was
completed. The journey time between Montreal and Port Moody, British Columbia, was estimated to be five or six days.
1917 : Russian Bolsheviks under LENIN overthrew the
provisional government of ALEXANDER KERENSKY in Petrograd.
1921 : The 38-year-old son of a blacksmith became
official leader of the 35 parliamentary members of Italy's National Fascist Party. BENITO MUSSOLINI was a socialist before World War one but moved to the right during and after the war.
1929 : The British government warned it would ban
vehicles capable of speeds of 60 miles an hour and over.
1938 : A Polish Jew killed German diplomat ERNST VON RATH

in Paris. The young gunman was protesting at the Nazi expulsions of Jews. The shooting was followed by what was said to be a spontaneous reaction from the German people. Jewish communities throughout Germany were subjected to a "reign of terror". Jews were murdered, their shops were looted and hundreds of synagogues were burnt down. In the following days further retribution was handed out. Jews were expelled from colleges and HITLER fined the Jewish community one billion marks for VON RATH's death.
1950 : In the first ever combat between jet fighters a
U.S. F86 shot down a MIG 15 over Korea.
1963 : The United States recognised the new South
Vietnamese government.
1974 : Lord LUCAN disappeared after allegedly bashing his

children's nanny to death. There were reports that he had comitted suicide but police files have not been closed on the case. In 1978 there were reported sightings of Lord LUCAN in Melbourne, Holland, Dublin and Johannesburg, some
simultaneously.
1980 : American actor STEVE McQUEEN died. His Hollywood
films included "The Great Escape".
1990 : A man fired two shots from a hunting rifle during

the October Revolution anniversary parade in Moscow's Red Square. Police spotted the man aiming at the reviewing stand on top of the Lenin Mausoleum where President GORBACHEV was taking the salute. Police wrestled the gunman to the ground. ALEXANDR SHIMONOV was charged with attempting a terrorist act.
